LESSON: WEALTH, MONEY AND POVERTY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Christian Living Today
Topic 5.4: Wealth, Money and Poverty

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Wealth, Money and Poverty. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which vices are associated with love for money?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WEALTH, MONEY AND POVERTY
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Wealth, Money and Poverty helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

PART 1: Discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Wealth, Money and Poverty” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Wealth, Money and Poverty is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Wealth, Money and Poverty” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Wealth, Money and Poverty to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Wealth, Money and Poverty from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Wealth, Money and Poverty: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Wealth, Money and Poverty?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which vices are associated with love for money?
2. Why is integrity important in handling money and wealth?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Wealth, Money and Poverty means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: discuss Christian teachings on wealth, money, and poverty.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
